preconditions: an erosion surface and its event order are explicit
the depositional environment is classified as fluvial, estuarine, marine-influenced, glacial, or unresolved
subunit thicknesses share one section coordinate system and length unit
every non-synthetic parameter is bound to evidence whose spatial and temporal scope contains the model request
eventLogic: Construct the valley erosion surface independently of the later fill contacts.
Place the first fill subunit on the erosion surface.
Place each later subunit on the exact active top of its predecessor; later deposition must not re-erode earlier fill unless a separate erosion event is declared.
Clip all fill subunits to the valley accommodation space and permit marginal pinch-out to zero thickness.
Do not require basal gravel everywhere: observed Japanese valleys include cases where it is absent.
Choose allowed facies and transitions from the classified environment; do not use one global fixed sequence.

mathematicalContracts.stacking: B_1(x)=E(x); B_i(x)=T_{i-1}(x) for i>1; T_i(x)=min(B_i(x)+H_i(x), A(x)); H_i(x)>=0
mathematicalContracts.exclusivePartition: For every in-domain point, active fill interiors are pairwise disjoint and their union equals the declared filled portion of [E(x),A(x)].
mathematicalContracts.transitionProbability: t_jk(h)=P{F(x+h)=k | F(x)=j}; estimate separately for each direction and compatible environment/process group.
mathematicalContracts.gaussianSuperposition: If independent zero-mean Gaussian components G_q are used as a synthetic surface primitive, S=sum_q w_q G_q has covariance C_S=sum_q w_q^2 C_q. This identity does not supply geological ranges, weights, asymmetry, or valley morphology.

requiredEvidence: erosion-surface or valley-base evidence, or SyntheticAssumption status
direction-specific transition evidence when a transition matrix is used
thickness/range/weight evidence or explicit SyntheticAssumption status
exclusions: using vertical borehole transitions as measured lateral transitions
reusing the original erosion surface as the bottom of every fill subunit
creating asymmetry by an undocumented one-sided multiplier
claiming that a sum of Gaussian fields is itself evidence of a real valley morphology
authorizing a real region from terrain or surface geology alone
uncertainty: Facies order, continuity, proportions, transition matrices, surface ranges and asymmetry remain environment- and dataset-conditioned. Synthetic values remain SyntheticAssumption.
validationMethod: positive: multi-subunit fill stacks without gap or overlap
boundary: one or more subunits pinch out at a valley margin
negative: a later subunit using the erosion surface again is rejected as overlap
missing-data: absent environment classification prevents a literature-derived sequence
conflicting-evidence: mutually incompatible environment profiles are not pooled
out-of-scope: coastal transgressive succession is rejected for an unclassified mountain valley
directionality: vertical and lateral transition evidence cannot be silently interchanged
reopenCondition: Implementing a real regional profile, a calibrated asymmetric erosion-surface model, or a transition simulator
